subtype: Blank face at bullying or shame [Regulating]
passage:
“How was school?” asked Dhruv, dropping his bag.
“Fine,” said Yogesh, his face flat as a wall.
“Your face is doing the wall thing. Did somebody say something?”
Yogesh looked at the floor. “They call me Stick. I just look at nothing so they get bored.”
“Does it work?”
“A bit. It also feels like a stone in my stomach.”
“I'm glad you told me. Want me to come and talk to Sir?”
“Maybe. Not yet.”
“Okay. I'll ask again tomorrow.”

qa.q: What do the boys call Yogesh?
What is Yogesh feeling behind his blank face?
qa.a: Hurt, and probably ashamed, since he says it feels like a stone in his stomach. He keeps his face still so the boys get bored and stop.
Respect Yogesh's pace, keep checking in, and be ready to go with him to talk to Sir when he is ready.

qa.q: How might Dhruv see his brother's blank face?
qa.a: He can tell it is not calm, since he calls it “the wall thing”, so he is probably worried and wants to help.

grounding: A child keeps a blank face when teased; an adult checks in privately and offers help.

subtype: Blank face at bullying or shame [Regulating]
passage: I'm Dilnaz. When the girls at the bus stop laughed about my haircut, I made my face like a stone. I didn't blink or smile. Inside I was shaking. At lunch I didn't eat, and Maria Ma'am, my class teacher, noticed. She sat down beside me and said quietly, “The bus stop seemed hard today. You can tell me, or you can help me with the library books. Either is fine.” I chose the books. After a while I said, “They laughed at my hair.” She said, “Thank you for telling me. You can come to me any time.”

qa.q: What did Maria Ma'am ask Dilnaz to help with as an alternative to talking?
qa.a: She offered that Dilnaz could help her with the library books.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling behind her stone face?
qa.a: Hurt and ashamed, since she says inside she was shaking. She kept her face blank so as not to give the girls a reaction.

qa.q: What did Maria Ma'am do that made it easier to talk?
qa.a: She spoke quietly and privately, gave Dilnaz a choice and an easy task, and said she could come any time.

qa.q: How might the girls at the bus stop have read Dilnaz's stone face?
qa.a: They may have thought she did not care, and not seen the hurt behind it.

grounding: A child holds a blank face when teased, which hides real hurt; a private check-in helps.
